passages.heading: Overview
passages.chapter: Chapter 3. Recommend Career Management Self-Development
passages.body:
1. Leadership. The demanding, politically sensitive, and often high-risk nature of missions that Special Forces Soldiers perform requires extremely competent Noncommissioned Officers that can succeed in an increasingly complex and dynamic contemporary operational environment. Therefore, the Special Forces branch naturally produces a high concentration of highly skilled Noncommissioned Officers. Those Noncommissioned Officers that consistently exceed standards and demonstrate mental and physical capabilities above their peers are more competitive for demanding positions and career advancement. Leaders, the Special Forces Proponent, the United States Army Human Resources Command, and the Noncommissioned Officer Professional Development System (NCOPDS) all play an essential part in the career development of the force; however, each Soldier is ultimately the true steward of their career. Noncommissioned Officers at every rank are encouraged to demonstrate their ability to exceed standards in character, presence, intellect, leads, develops, and achieves by setting the example for their peers and subordinates through personal courage, confidence, competence, military bearing, general military knowledge, and warrior skills. To assist leaders with talent management, Noncommissioned Officers at every level must seek opportunities to demonstrate their leadership potential and distinguish themselves from their peers. NOTE: Regarding Senior Rater comments on NCOERs, the phrase “#1 selection for promotion” should be reserved for SMs in the top 5% of other NCOs in that grade who demonstrate Superior Performance and Potential. The phrase “Promote now/immediately” should be reserved for those SMs in the top 24% of NCOs of the same grade who demonstrate Outstanding Performance and Potential. The phrase “Promote with peers” should be used for those SMs who demonstrate Average Performance and Potential.
2. Physical Fitness. The ability to conduct Special Forces operations across the competition continuum requires Special Forces Soldiers to be of the highest physical capability for operating in the most rigorous environments. All personnel must maintain a high state of physical readiness. Physical fitness contributes to a Noncommissioned Officer’s overall wellness and ability to set the example for others. A holistic health and fitness (H2F) approach is essential to readiness when assessing a Soldier’s physical and mental status. Additionally, it assists to design programs to sustain or improve that Soldier’s ability to meet the demands of their MOSs, duty assignments, and combat-specific tasks. While it is a command responsibility to establish physical training policies and allocate sufficient resources for Soldiers to meet Army and unit standards and goals, it is an individual responsibility to meet those goals. All Soldiers are encouraged to use existing resources to assist them in making a healthy lifestyle, good dietary choices, and developing an individual goal-oriented physical training regimen. Special Forces Soldiers will meet all standards for their respective grades as specified in DA PAM 611-21 and IAW ATP 7- 22 scoring a minimum of 60 in each event and an overall score of at least 350 points. Noncommissioned Officers must meet all physical fitness requirements as directed by the command to ensure maximum mission readiness to fulfill global requirements with Joint special operations forces (SOF) partners. Must meet height and weigh IAW AR 600-9 or qualify for exception under current Army Directive.
3. Assignments. NCOs are encouraged to have a diverse career assignment profile. This covers a wide range of positions and duties pertaining to and outside of one’s MOS. A detailed list of Key Developmental, Nominative, Mission Critical, Mission Essential, and Mission Enhancing assignments can be found in Appendix A.
(a) Key Developmental – Positions identified by the proponent as required to develop critical leadership and technical skills and experience that provide the greatest potential for advancement. Special Forces Proponent considers these positions to be on an SFOD-A, SFOD-E, SFOD-G, or in a Special Missions Unit (SMU). Company level positions such as those on a SFOD-B, SFOD-F, SFOD-H, and other company and Battalion positions, while important, are not considered Key Developmental positions. The Special Forces Regiment utilizes Professional Development Proficiency Codes (PDPCs) of 6H, 7H, and 8H at corresponding grades to denote completion of Key Development time.
(b) Key Billet Experience – Leaders may further optimize the distribution of NCO talent by selecting best qualified NCOs based on their Knowledge, Skills, and Behavior (KSBs) to key positions across the enterprise. These positions are designated for experienced leaders of character who demonstrate potential and have proven their competence in a broad range of environments. Positive performance in key billets should signal superior performance and potential.
(1) Nominative – Nominative positions provide significantly elevated leadership experience, institutional/unit management responsibilities, and regular engagement and reporting to higher echelons of command at or beyond key responsibilities at the next rank and grade. These positions provide significant leadership experience to best prepare Soldiers for successful service in the next grade and beyond. These positions require packet submissions approved by Special Forces Group (or higher) CSMs and should be filled from the top 5% of Special Forces NCOs within the Regiment.
(2) Mission Critical – Mission critical positions provide elevated direct and indirect leadership experience, training management responsibilities, and regular engagement and reporting to higher echelons of command corresponding with key responsibilities at the next rank and grade. These positions provide additional leadership experience to better prepare Soldiers for successful service in the next grade. These positions should be filled from the top 24% of Special Forces NCOs within the Regiment.
(3) Mission Essential – These positions are required to conduct force generation, advanced training, and other staff functions.
4. Military Education
(a) Professional Military Education: NOTE: Obtaining recognition as the Distinguished Honor Graduate, Honor Graduate, Commandant’s List, or Leadership Awardee at Professional Military Education (PME) courses, or any MOS enhancing courses attended should be the goal of all Special Forces NCOs.
(b) Functional and Institutional Domain Training: Special Forces Noncommissioned Officers should pursue formal military training opportunities that improve their survivability, tactical, and technical skills and increase their ability to lead Soldiers in any Special Forces unit that they may be assigned. This includes but is not limited to all Additional Skill Identifier (ASI), Special Qualifications Identifier (SQI), and Professional Development Skill Identifier Producing Schools (PDSI), Joint Service Courses, and International Military/Government Training. See Appendix C for a list of courses, ASIs, SQIs, and PDSIs pertaining to CMF 18 NCOs. Soldiers interested in challenging themselves and setting themselves ahead of their peer group should compete in competitions such as the U.S. Army Best Medic Competition, U.S. Army Best Ranger Competition, U.S. Army Best Sapper Competition, U.S. Army Best Warrior/Best Squad Competition, U.S. Army Best Sniper Competition, USASOC Best Sniper Competition, Soldier and Non-Commissioned Officer of the Month, Quarter, and Year boards, and other similar competitions. NCOs at every rank are encouraged to compete for acceptance into the Sergeant Audie Murphy Club. Soldiers of all ranks are highly encouraged to continue their military training and education through self-paced and distributed-learning platforms. Courses in a wide variety of military topics can be found at the Army Learning Management System (ALMS), Joint Knowledge Online (JKO), and the Joint Special Operations University (JSOU).
5. Language Proficiency and Regional Expertise. Maintaining language proficiency, cultural expertise, knowledge of issues, and trends are a critical role within the Special Forces mission to better engage, understand, and influence partners within the operational environment. Individuals must take every opportunity to improve their knowledge and understanding of their aligned region's history and current affairs. See Appendix D for a list of languages by category and code.
6. Civilian Education. Civilian (academic) education is a component of the self-development program for Special Forces Soldiers. Early career management accelerates professional development and allows for flexibility in operational requirements and tempo. A college degree is not required for promotion, but it should look favorable, and it can be a deciding factor in identifying the Most Qualified (Superior Performance and Potential) NCOs. Soldiers are encouraged to pursue a degree or certificate program that relates to their MOS to receive maximum credit for previous military training. Soldiers should seek more information on this topic by utilizing the Service-member Opportunity Colleges Army Degree (SOCAD) website https://www.education.army.mil/socad.aspx. See Appendix E for more information on how to obtain college credits.

Should set their educational goal of completing a bachelor’s degree. Due to limited authorizations and fiercely competitive records, civilian education may be considered a major factor for selection to Command Sergeant Major (CSM) positions.
7. Jumpmaster. All Critical Leadership Development opportunities are airborne assignments. All active-duty Special Forces NCOs should attend the Static Line or Military Free-Fall Jumpmaster Course at the earliest opportunity.
8. Army Career Tracker (ACT). ACT is a leadership development tool that integrates training and education into one personalized, easy-to-use website. Users can search multiple Army education and training resources, monitor their career development, and receive personalized advice from their supervisor, Army leadership, and individually selected mentors. The chain of command and the Noncommissioned Officer support channel assist Soldiers in managing their careers through counseling, mentoring, and coaching. Leaders should also assist Soldiers in establishing an individual development plan within the ACT website. The College of the American Soldier, accessible through the career resources tab on the Army Career Tracker (ACT) is designed to expand existing civilian education choices for Soldiers to provide them with degree options that will enhance their leadership capabilities while maximizing college credit granted for military experience.
9. Professional Reading. Special Forces Soldiers of all ranks should pursue self-development and understanding of the Army profession through professional reading. Special Forces NCOs of all ranks should read titles from the Sergeant Major of Army’s recommended reading list which can be found at the Association of the United States Army website: https://www.ausa.org/programs/nco-and-soldiers/sma-weimer-reading- list. A list of military publications Special Forces NCOs should all be familiar with is in Appendix F.

passages.chapter: Chapter 4. MOS 18B, 18C, 18D, 18E, 18F, and 18Z: Special Forces Weapons, Engineer, Medical, Communications, Intelligence, Team, and Operations Sergeants
passages.body: Special Forces branch guidance is for Noncommissioned Officers to serve in Key Development positions to be considered minimally MOS qualified (MMQ). SF NCOs should serve in a variety of institutional and operational billets throughout their career to increase their development. Professional Development Models for MOS 18B, 18C, 18D, 18E, 18F, and 18Z are available at https://actnow.army.mil; and on the Army HRC website at https://www.hrc.army.mil/content/CMF%2018%20Information. NOTE: Proponent guidance should not be construed as a simplified checklist for promotion selection. It does not guarantee promotion or a competitive Order of Merit (OML) number following the Evaluation Boards. NCOs who have completed assignments in Key Development positions and consistently outperformed their peers with supporting rater and senior rater comments are viewed more favorably by board members.

passages.body: MOS 18Z5 Special Forces Team Sergeant CMF18 Master Sergeants are considered minimally MOS Qualified (MMQ) and eligible to be awarded PDPC-ASI “8H” with a total of 24 months key development as defined in Appendix A: Key Developmental Assignments. 12 months must be served as a MSG. NOTE: While NCOs who have served as a SFOD-A/E/G or SMU Team Sergeant as a SFC have demonstrated progression ahead of their peers, up to one year of SFC Team Sergeant time can be considered as Key Developmental time. Example: A NCO served 18 months as a SFC Team Sergeant and promotes to MSG. The NCO must complete an additional 12 months as a Team Sergeant to be awarded the PDPC-ASI “8H” and be considered Key Development complete.

(e) Military Supervisory Skill: Must have one supervisory skillset in Appendix B2. Should be a Jumpmaster
(f) Civilian Education: Should set their educational goal of enrolling in bachelor’s degree.
(g) Language: Should meet the language proficiency standard (per AR 11-6, 1-15 m and USASOC Reg 350-1, 4-5 a) by scoring a 1+ on the Oral Proficiency Interview (16 in Speaking) or 1+/1+ on the Defense Language Proficiency Test (16 in Reading and 16 in Listening) within 12 months as reflected on the Soldier Talent Profile.

(1) 24 months as a SFOD-A/E/G or SMU Team Sergeant; and rated time in a mission critical position.
(2) 36 months as a SFOD-A/E/G or SMU Team Sergeant. NOTE: The SMU SF MSG must successfully serve no less than 48 months within the SMU and possess SQI-T or serve as a SMU Case Officer.
(b) Assignments
(1) Key Developmental Assignments: See Appendix A
(2) Mission Critical Assignments: See Appendix A (PDSI L3B)
(c) Physical Fitness: Must pass the AFT with a total score of 450 or more. Must meet Height and Weight IAW AR 600-9.
(d) Military Education: Must be a Master Leader Course Graduate for Sergeants Major Academy selection. Must have one or more advanced skills (See Appendix B1). (f) Civilian Education: Should set their educational goal of enrolling in bachelor’s degree.
(g) Language: Should meet the language proficiency standard (per AR 11-6, 1-15 m and USASOC Reg 350-1, 4-5 a) by scoring a 1+ on the Oral Proficiency Interview (16 in Speaking) or 1+/1+ on the Defense Language Proficiency Test (16 in Reading and 16 in Listening) within 12 months as reflected on the Soldier Talent Profile.
3. Fully Qualified
(a) Leadership: Must be a MSG. Must be serving in a Mission Essential Billet (See Appendix A). Must meet criteria as outlined in corresponding FY HRC MILPER MSG Evaluation Board Announcement Message.
(b) Physical Fitness: Must pass the AFT with a total score of 410 or be on a current profile. Must score 80 points on the MDL, HRP, SDC, and PLK, and 90 points in the 2MR in the M/C category in the soldier’s age group. Must meet Height and Weight IAW AR 600-9.
(c) Military Education: Must be a Master Leader Course Graduate for Sergeants Major Academy selection
4. Not Fully Qualified
(a) Leadership: Received one of the following in the last 12 months in current grade:
(1) General Officer Memorandum of Reprimand (GOMAR)
(2) Relief for Cause NCOER
(3) Annotation of “Did Not Meet Standard” in Part IV (Performance Evaluation, Professionalism, Attributes, and Competencies), block c (Character)
(4) Annotation of “Not Qualified” in Part V (Senior Rater Overall Potential), block a (Rated Noncommissioned Officer’s Potential)

passages.chapter: Chapter 4. MOS 18B, 18C, 18D, 18E, 18F, and 18Z: Special Forces Weapons, Engineer, Medical, Communications, Intelligence, Team, and Operations Sergeants
passages.body: Special Forces branch guidance is for Noncommissioned Officers to serve in Key Development positions to be considered minimally MOS qualified (MMQ). SF NCOs should serve in a variety of institutional and operational billets throughout their career to increase their development. Professional Development Models for MOS 18B, 18C, 18D, 18E, 18F, and 18Z are available at https://actnow.army.mil; and on the Army HRC website at https://www.hrc.army.mil/content/CMF%2018%20Information. NOTE: Proponent guidance should not be construed as a simplified checklist for promotion selection. It does not guarantee promotion or a competitive Order of Merit (OML) number following the Evaluation Boards. NCOs who have completed assignments in Key Development positions and consistently outperformed their peers with supporting rater and senior rater comments are viewed more favorably by board members.

passages.body: MOS 18Z5 Special Forces Team Sergeant CMF18 Master Sergeants are considered minimally MOS Qualified (MMQ) and eligible to be awarded PDPC-ASI “8H” with a total of 24 months key development as defined in Appendix A: Key Developmental Assignments. 12 months must be served as a MSG. NOTE: While NCOs who have served as a SFOD-A/E/G or SMU Team Sergeant as a SFC have demonstrated progression ahead of their peers, up to one year of SFC Team Sergeant time can be considered as Key Developmental time. Example: A NCO served 18 months as a SFC Team Sergeant and promotes to MSG. The NCO must complete an additional 12 months as a Team Sergeant to be awarded the PDPC-ASI “8H” and be considered Key Development complete.

passages.heading: Master Sergeant (MSG) — promotion consideration

passages.body:

Must have 24 months as a SFOD-A/E/G or SMU Team Sergeant; and rated time in a nominative position. passages.heading: Sergeant First Class — assignments (appendix; applies to every MOS in this chapter)
passages.chapter: Chapter 4-app1. Appendix A – Assignments
passages.body:
(a) Key Developmental (ASI 7H): - 24 months as a SFC on a SFOD-A/E/G, SMU, SWCS SR INSTR/WTR, Nominative, and/or Mission Critical Position (Note: above positions can be combined to total 24 months)
(b) Nominative (PDSI L3C): - SFOD-A/E/G or SMU TM SGT - Special Forces Proponent Personnel Career Manager - HRC Career Management NCO - Any SFC filling a nominative or mission critical MSG billet
(c) Mission Critical (PDSI L3D): - Team NCOIC at Robin Sage, MOS, SUT, and SFAS - NCOA Senior Instructor/Writer - Any SFC filling a TOE/TDA 18Z5 position.
(d) Mission Essential: All other SFC positions not previously listed.

passages.heading: Master Sergeant / First Sergeant — assignments (appendix; applies to every MOS in this chapter)
passages.chapter: Chapter 4-app1. Appendix A – Assignments
passages.body:
(a) Key Developmental (ASI 8H): - 24 months as a Team Sergeant on a SFOD-A/E/G, or SMU (12 months must be served as a MSG)
(b) Nominative (PDSI L3A): - Special Forces Proponent Personnel Senior Career Manager - HRC Senior Talent Management NCO - A/4/1 SWTG(A) 1SG - HHC 1SG at Special Forces Group - HHC 1SG at USASOC, USAJFKSWCS, or 1st SFC(A) - 18A 1SG or Chief Instructor/Writer - NCOA 1SG - Any MSG filling a nominative or critical SGM billet.
(c) Mission Critical (PDSI L3B): - All other 1SG positions - J3 Operations SGT at TSOC - S3 Operations SGT at Special Forces Group (Group level) - SFPC, SFAS, or Any Phase of SFQC Chief Instructor/Writer - Any NCOA Chief instructor/Writer - Any ASI or SQI producing Chief Instructor/Writer
(d) Mission Essential: - All other MSG positions not previously listed.

passages.heading: Sergeant Major — assignments (appendix; applies to every MOS in this chapter)
passages.chapter: Chapter 4-app1. Appendix A – Assignments
passages.body:
(a) Key Developmental: - 12 months as Special Forces Company SGM or SMU SGM. (Note 1: position can be filled by a MSG who is a graduate of the USASMA, JSOFSEA, or equivalent course.) (Note 2: Key Development time can be completed as a MSG as long as they are a graduate of the USASMA, JSOFSEA, or equivalent course)
(b) Nominative: - SFAS SGM - SF Proponent SGM - HRC TADD ARSOF Division SGM - G3 SGM at USASOC, USAJFKSWCS, or 1 st SFC(A) G3 SGM - J3 SGM at TSOC - S3 SGM at Special Forces Group or Special Warfare Training Group
(c) Mission Critical: - S3 SGM at Special Forces Group (Battalion level) - Company SGM at any phase of SFQC - SGM at G8, IG, or SMU
(d) Mission Essential: - All other SGM positions not previously listed.
